python3 - <<'PY'
import re, pathlib
path = pathlib.Path('tests/codegen/io/streams.rs')
text = path.read_text()

# A continuation line carrying only `.stderr` has no receiver on it, so the receiver-anchored
# rename could not see it. Scope it to the one test that spells its access that way.
old = """    assert_eq!(
        modern
            .stderr
            .matches("the $escape parameter must be provided")"""
new = """    assert_eq!(
        modern
            .diagnostics
            .matches("the $escape parameter must be provided")"""
assert text.count(old) == 1
text = text.replace(old, new)

# The prose predates the move: the notice now travels on php's stdout diagnostic funnel.
old_doc = """/// `--php-version`, which makes a program built for 8.3 noisier than the interpreter it is
/// asked to imitate. stderr is what has to be inspected — the notice never touches stdout, so
/// a stdout-only check reads the same for a gate that works and a gate that is missing."""
new_doc = """/// `--php-version`, which makes a program built for 8.3 noisier than the interpreter it is
/// asked to imitate. The DIAGNOSTIC stream is what has to be inspected — the notice never
/// reaches the program's own output, so a stdout-only check reads the same for a gate that
/// works and a gate that is missing."""
assert text.count(old_doc) == 1
text = text.replace(old_doc, new_doc)

path.write_text(text)
print("fixed")
